newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
GUJRAL SAYS LALOO YADAV SHOULD RESIGN

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said when people holding public offices faced charges of corruption they should give up their offices. "I will not name anyone in particular. All corrupt persons be it politicians or bureaucrats will not be spared. What is more important is if a minister becomes corrupt action has to be taken against him and we will do so," he said at a public meeting. He said the ruling United Front would not compromise on corruption and fight it at all costs. Gujral also said there was no difference of opinion between him and the leftist parties on the issue.
The Economic Times
BOMBAY SENSITIVE INDEX UP BY 98.3 POINTS

Cash shares flared up Wednesday on the Bombay bourse because of heavy purchases by operators and traders who anticipated the return of the retail investors. The sensitive index shot up by 98 points to touch 4,404.69 points. With this, the index has jumped 570 points in four weeks. It is now about 240 points below the all-time high of 4,643 points recorded in September 1994. Sustained purchases by foreign institutional investors in heavyweight stocks also contributed to the rise.
NO PUBLIC ISSUE FOR BUYBACK OF SHARES

Companies should not be allowed public issues of shares to buy them back, a Securities and Exchange Board of India committee said. Companies planning to buy back shares should offer them to shareholders on a proportionate basis before buying the shares from the open market. Buying back should be restricted to shares alone and not be applicable to securities. Companies should not be allowed to use the money collected from an earlier issue to buy its own shares.
GOVERNMENT LOOKING FOR WHITE KNIGHTS

The government is looking for white knights who can save a number of its loss-making companies in return for a good chunk of equity. The companies include Bharat Heavy Plates and Vessels, Bharat Pumps and Compressors, Bridge and Roof Company, Tungabhadra Steel Products, Praga Tools, Hindustan Salts, Bharat Leather, Andrew Yule, National Industrial Development Corporation and Scooters India. Many of these companies have stopped commercial functioning and are depending heavily on government props to survive.
Financial Express
EUROISSUE ROADSHOWS BY POWER FINANCE CORP

The Power Finance Corporation plans to conduct roadshows in the international market for a proposed $125 million Euroissue. ING Barings, lead managers to the issue, will inform investors about it. A senior official of the corporation said funds would be raised through Eurobonds. The chairman of the company will lead a team to Hong Kong, the United States and many European countries. The roadshow will be kicked off from Hong Kong. The corporation is waiting for the Finance Ministry's approval.
U.S. SARA LEE PICKS UP MAJORITY STAKE IN GODREJ HICARE

Sara Lee Corporation of the United States has acquired a majority stake in Godrej HIcare, a joint venture between the Bombay-based Godrej group and Sara Lee. Sara Lee paid Godrej Soaps 550 million rupees for 11 percent of Godrej HIcare's stake. The managing director of the Godrej HIcare declined to comment.
Business Standard
FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVES TO DROP

The Reserve Bank of India will revalue its gold reserves downward in line with the crash in international gold prices. As a result, foreign exchange reserves will drop below $29 billion. It will also affect the RBI's balance sheet as on June 30, 1997. The RBI's gold reserves were valued at $4.4 billion in June 1996. This will drop by at least $800 million. The RBI values its gold stock at the end of each month at 90 percent of the month's daily average London price. The rupee equivalent is determined on the basis of the exchange rate at the end of the month.
NO BANK DEALS WITH UNREGISTERED FINANCE FIRMS

The Reserve Bank has decided in principle to direct all banks to cut off transactions with non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) that have not registered with it. A circular on this is expected soon. Once this is done, the NBFCs that have not registered with the Reserve Bank will not be able to do any business even if they have registered with the registrar of companies. The last day for NBFCs to register with the Reserve Bank was July 8. A senior Reserve Bank official said the bank was planning to implement the decision soon in an attempt to regulate unregistered NBFCs.
The Observer
LIBERAL NORMS FOR EXPORT-ORIENTED FIRMS

The government on Wednesday included sub-contracting and private bonded warehouses in the automatic approval list of 100 percent export-oriented units. Sub-contractors will now qualify for automatic approval provided they conform to the parameters laid down by the government in 1995 and allowed as per the Customs Department guidelines, an official statement said. The 1995 order says that for automatic approval, the entire manufacturing operations of such units should be carried out on the same premises and the proposal should not envisage sub-contracting by sending any raw materials for further manufacturing outside the premises.
